approach: Since the straw's wall has negligible thickness, the liquid meets it along two contact lines, one inside and one outside, each pulling with surface tension at the contact angle.

steps.text: Write the length of one contact line where the liquid meets the circular wall of the straw.
Because the wall has negligible thickness, the liquid touches it from inside and from outside, giving two such contact lines.
steps.why_this_step: A real straw has two surfaces facing the liquid at almost the same radius, so both menisci pull on it.

steps.text: Write the total force from surface tension, resolved along the vertical using the contact angle.
Simplify to match the form of the options.

common_mistakes.text: Counting only one contact line, inside or outside, instead of both gives 6πRT/5.
Forgetting to resolve the surface tension force through the contact angle, taking cos53° as 1, gives 4πRT, which is not among the printed options.
